evidence_note: This is the Parasari (BPHS-descended) delineation layer, distinct from and not merged with the Jaimini sign-based track at docs/research/multitradition/jaimini/. Every rule below is paraphrased (not quoted at length) from V. Subrahmanya Sastri's 1950 second-edition English translation of Mantreswara's Phaladeepika (archive item in.gov.ignca.6945, registry jyotisha_mantreswara_phaladeepika_subrahmanya_1950_archive). That scan's title page states 'copyright registered' and the item's Archive metadata leaves the rights field empty, so this pack is treated exactly as the existing brhajjataka_planetary_rule_manifest.json treats Aiyar's 1905 Brhajjataka translation: internal alignment and paraphrase research, not a customer-facing quotation, pending a jurisdictional rights decision. The same scan carries Devanagari sloka text before each translated passage, but djvu OCR of that Devanagari is corrupted in this copy (mixed Latin/Devanagari misreads) and could not be used to control wording independently; no direct Sanskrit rendering is offered here, and none is claimed. Sloka numbers are read directly off the OCR's own 'Sloka N' labels adjacent to each passage and are corroborated against the printed table of contents and descriptive contents (both inspected), not invented. Chapter (Adhyaya) attributions for the yoga passages are read from the nearest running-header page marker ('Adh. V/VI/VII') in the same scan; where two chapters' headers appear within a few pages of a passage, both are named and the uncertainty is disclosed rather than silently resolved. Every planet-in-bhava and dasha-result table below is a paraphrase lookup, matching the compact 'directed_relationship_lookup' / lookup-table convention already used in brhajjataka_planetary_rule_manifest.json, rather than one rule object per clause. No numeric strength (Shadbala/Ashtakavarga), muhurta timing, remedial prescription, marriage-compatibility, or lifespan claim is encoded anywhere in this file, consistent with the tradition's refusal list. Progeny/children counts stated by the source for some houses and yogas are retained here as historical testimony (kind: topical_verdict) but are flagged output_policy: suppress-as-fertility-adjacent, matching the corpus's existing treatment of varna/caste material - retain in the research trace, never render as a claim about a living person's fertility. Nothing in this file is customer-eligible; customer_prediction is false throughout and no composer or engine code was written to consume it.

conclusion.recovery_note: Houses 1-7 recovered and now PAGE-IMAGE VERIFIED from the second witness. The pack's primary scan (in.gov.ignca.6945) is physically defective: it jumps from leaf 117 (printed p. 81, end of Adhyaya VII) straight to printed p. 84 (leaf 118), so printed pp. 82-83 - the Adhyaya VIII opening and slokas 1-3 - were never scanned. dli.ernet.507316 leaves 0114-0115 (printed pp. 82-83) supply them. Same work, same translator, a different scan: a scan repair, NOT a cross-author substitution, which the corpus forbids. Houses 8-12 (sloka 3 tail and sloka 4) verified on the primary witness leaf 0118 (printed p. 84), where the print reads '8th house' at the point the OCR misread as '6th'.

exceptions: Sloka 1's house-1 result carries a sign-conditioned tail verified on the page images (dli.ernet.507316 pp. 82-83): if the Lagna the Sun occupies is Cancer he will have a cataract in the eyes; if Mesha, eye-disease; if Leo, night-blindness; if Libra, poverty and loss of children. These clauses are conditioned on the rasi, not the bhava, and are NOT folded into the unconditioned house-1 cell; the Libra clause is additionally progeny-adjacent and falls under this file's suppression policy.
Sun's own dignity/retrograde/combustion condition (already computed by the engine) is not folded into this table; the source states these as unconditioned bhava results, one line per house.

conditions.definition: one of Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus or Saturn occupies a kendra house (1st, 4th, 7th or 10th from the Lagna) identical with its own sign (swakshetra) or its exaltation sign (swoccha)

Mars.name: Ruchaka
Mars.result: a long face; acquires wealth by many daring deeds; brave; overcomes his enemies; powerful and arrogant; renowned for his merits; leader of an army; victorious in all his attempts

Mercury.name: Bhadra
Mercury.result: gifted with long life and keen intellect; clean; praised by the learned; leads men; very rich; clever in addressing an assembly

Jupiter.name: Hamsa
Jupiter.result: a king extolled by the good; auspicious marks (Sankha, Padma, Matsya, Ankusa) on the hands and feet; a beautiful body; eats sumptuous food; of righteous disposition

Venus.name: Malavya
Venus.result: strong limbs; resolute; wealthy; endowed with wife, children (suppressed) and good fortune; prosperous, eats well, enjoys pleasures, commands good vehicles; famous and learned; unperturbed senses

Saturn.name: Sasa
Saturn.result: extolled by all; good servants; strong; headman of a village or a king; wicked in disposition; has intrigues with women not his own; usurps others' wealth; happy

exceptions: Definition verse is printed as 'Sloka 1' of Adhyaya VI; the Ruchaka/Bhadra results are printed under 'Sloka 3' and the Hamsa/Malavya/Sasa results run from the tail of 'Sloka 3' into 'Sloka 4'; an intervening verse 2 was not needed for this rule and was not transcribed.

The engine already computes both dignity (own sign/exalted/debilitated/neutral) and whole-sign house from the Lagna, and already defines KENDRAS = (1,4,7,10) in src/engine/multitradition/vedic.py, so this rule's condition is directly checkable against existing computed facts - no new calculation is required, only composer wiring, which is out of scope for this research pass.

conditions.kesari: the Moon stands in a kendra house (1st, 4th, 7th or 10th) counted from Jupiter's own house
conditions.sakata: the Moon stands in the 12th, 8th or 6th house counted from Jupiter's own house
conditions.sakata_cancellation: Sakata does not arise if the Moon itself also occupies a kendra house (1st, 4th, 7th or 10th) from the Lagna

conclusion.kesari_result: destroys all his enemies like a lion; speaks loftily and nobly in an assembly; passionate and emotional in behaviour; long-lived; highly renowned; exceedingly intelligent; conquers everything by his own valour
conclusion.sakata_result: often becomes unfortunate and may regain what he once lost; a very ordinary and insignificant man; attains much inevitable mental grief; exceedingly unhappy

exceptions: 'Kendra counted from Jupiter' (or from the Moon) is a relative-house count between two grahas, distinct from the engine's current house-from-Lagna computation; the underlying fact (each graha's whole-sign house) is already computed, so the relative count itself is arithmetic on existing facts (a kendra from graha X is houses whose whole-sign distance from X's house is 0, 3, 6 or 9), but no composer logic currently evaluates it. This is the most commonly cited yoga in popular Parasari practice (usually called Gajakesari Yoga) and is flagged as the highest-value near-term addition.

conditions.adhama: the Moon occupies a kendra house (1st, 4th, 7th or 10th) counted from the Sun's own house
conditions.sama: the Moon occupies a panaphara house (2nd, 5th, 8th or 11th) counted from the Sun's own house
conditions.varishtha: the Moon occupies an apoklima house (3rd, 6th, 9th or 12th) counted from the Sun's own house

conclusion.graded_result: wealth, vehicles, fame, happiness, knowledge, intellectual precision, modesty, ability, learning, liberality and enjoyment are at their lowest under Adhama, middling under Sama, and highest under Varishtha

exceptions: This is a notable inversion of the usual convention that a kendra is the strongest relative position: here a kendra relation to the Sun (the tightest angular relation, closest to conjunction/combustion risk for the Moon) is graded WORST, and the loosest relation (apoklima) is graded BEST. This is the source's own stated ranking, not a transcription error, and must not be silently 'corrected' toward the usual kendra-is-strongest convention.
conflicts_with: a generic assumption that kendra placement is always the strongest classification in every Jyotisha context

conditions.sunapha: one or more grahas other than the Sun occupy the 2nd house counted from the Moon's own house
conditions.anapha: one or more grahas other than the Sun occupy the 12th house counted from the Moon's own house
conditions.durudhara: grahas other than the Sun occupy both the 2nd and the 12th house counted from the Moon
conditions.kemadruma: none of the above three configurations is present
conditions.kemadruma_dissenting_view: some authorities named in the source hold that Kemadruma does not arise if the Moon is associated with any graha, or if a kendra house counted from the Moon is occupied by any graha - the source explicitly preserves this as a named minority position rather than resolving it

conclusion.sunapha_result: becomes a king or his equal, with self-acquired property, renowned for wisdom and wealth
conclusion.anapha_result: powerful, healthy, of amiable manners, known to fame, blessed with material comforts, well-dressed, contented and happy
conclusion.durudhara_result: freely takes to the joys of life as they arise; blessed with abundance of wealth and vehicles; bountiful; waited upon by faithful attendants
conclusion.kemadruma_result: even one of a princely race becomes obscure, miserable, given to base ways, penurious, drudging as a menial, and wickedly disposed

exceptions: This is a relative-house-from-the-Moon computation, not from the Lagna; src/engine/multitradition/vedic.py currently computes whole-sign house only from the Lagna (see `_graha_row`'s `house` field), so no composer logic can evaluate Sunapha/Anapha/Durudhara/Kemadruma against the live engine's current facts without first adding a house-from-the-Moon (chandra lagna) reckoning. This is flagged as a concrete, scoped engine extension, not merely a sourcing gap.
The dissenting Kemadruma-cancellation view is preserved as a named alternative and must not be silently adopted or silently discarded.

conditions.subhavesi_papavesi: benefic(s) [Subhavesi] or malefic(s) [Papavesi] other than the Moon occupy the 2nd house counted from the Sun
conditions.subhavaasi_paapavaasi: benefic(s) or malefic(s) other than the Moon occupy the 12th house counted from the Sun

conclusion.subhavesi_result: very handsome, happy, a store of merit, brave, a king, virtuous
conclusion.asubhavesi_result: unjustly vilifies others; loses his splendour; associates with the low; wicked
conclusion.subhavaasi_result: famous, liked by all, exceedingly prosperous, liberal, favourite of the sovereign
conclusion.asubhavaasi_result: deceitful; abuses others; befriends the wicked; of unrighteous conduct though he quotes scripture
conclusion.subhobhayachari_result: has beautiful limbs; affable in address; delights the world; eloquent in speech; renowned and wealthy
conclusion.paapobhayachari_result: mentally afflicted owing to public dishonour; bereft of learning, wealth and luck
conclusion.subhakartari_result: long-lived; fearless; free from disease; without enemies; happy and rich
conclusion.papakartari_result: poor; impure; unhappy; bereft of wife and children (suppressed); deprived of some limb; short-lived

exceptions: The Lagna-relative sub-cases (Subhakartari/Papakartari, Susubha) use house-from-Lagna, which the engine already computes; the Sun-relative sub-cases (Subhavesi/Papavesi/Subhavaasi/Paapavaasi/-obhayachari) require house-from-the-Sun, which the engine does not currently compute (a narrower cousin of the Sunapha-family gap above).

The exact Sanskrit names for the benefic/malefic Vaasi and Obhayachari pairs are uncertain in this OCR (the Devanagari is corrupted); the English descriptive labels used here follow the translator's own English gloss where the transliterated name could not be confirmed.

conditions.rajayoga_1: malefics are posited in the 3rd, 6th and 11th houses counted from the house occupied by the lord of the Lagna, or from the house occupied by the lord of the Janma Rasi (the Moon's sign)

conclusion.judgment: each of these four configurations is declared a Raja Yoga by 'those versed in the science'; the source does not further differentiate their relative strength against one another

exceptions: Rajayoga 4's phrasing ('quartered in the 10th, 11th and the Lagna') is read as one graha occupying each of the three named houses, not all three grahas occupying one house together; a facsimile check should confirm this reading.

conditions.trigger: a graha occupies its own sign of debilitation (dignity = debilitated, per the engine's existing dignity computation)
cancellation_test_any_of: the lord of that debilitation sign occupies a kendra (1st, 4th, 7th or 10th) counted from the Lagna
the lord of that debilitation sign occupies a kendra counted from the Moon
the lord of the debilitated graha's own exaltation sign occupies a kendra counted from the Lagna
the lord of the debilitated graha's own exaltation sign occupies a kendra counted from the Moon
conditions.reciprocal_intensifier: if the kendra relation between the two relevant lords is mutual (each stands in a kendra from the other), the resulting rank is higher than a one-directional case
conditions.weaker_intensifier: if the debilitation-sign lord merely aspects (rather than co-occupies a kendra with) the debilitated graha, a weaker grade of the same cancellation is produced; if the debilitated graha additionally sits in a house other than the 6th, 8th or 12th, that weaker grade is itself upgraded

conclusion.one_directional_result: the person born will become a king and a just ruler
conclusion.mutual_result: the person becomes an emperor respected by all other kings
conclusion.merely_aspected_result: the person becomes a ruler of the earth and famous; if the debilitated graha also stands in a house other than the 6th, 8th or 12th, this is upgraded to a foremost king
conclusion.full_form_result: the person becomes an emperor endowed with full riches, virtuously disposed, respected by other kings, mighty, famous and affluent
conclusion.adjacent_related_rule: if exactly one of the lords of the 11th, 9th and 2nd houses occupies a kendra with respect to the Moon, and Jupiter happens to be the lord of the 2nd, 5th or 11th house, the person becomes the ruler of a full-blown empire (Sloka 25, printed immediately before the Neechabhanga passage and grouped with it in the source)

exceptions: The kendra-from-Lagna branch of this rule is directly checkable against facts src/engine/multitradition/vedic.py already computes today: graha dignity (including 'debilitated'), house_lordships, and KENDRAS = (1,4,7,10). No new calculation is required for that branch.
The kendra-from-Moon branch requires the same house-from-the-Moon reckoning flagged as missing under the Sunapha/Anapha rule above; it is not yet checkable against the live engine.

This is the single most commonly cited 'exception' in popular Parasari practice (a planet in its fall is not automatically weak) and is flagged as the highest-value dignity-related composer addition in this pack.
conflicts_with: a flat rule that a debilitated graha is always weak with no cancellation test applied

results_by_graha.Sun_badly_placed_at_birth: promotes quarrel; sudden displeasure of the sovereign; sickness among relatives; wandering with others; intolerable mental anguish; danger from fire to concealed wealth, grain, sons and wife
results_by_graha.Sun_well_placed_at_birth: fame, success in undertakings, gravity, devotion to one's duty, and happiness
results_by_graha.Moon: acquisition of wealth through cruel deeds, kings and fighting; gain through medicines, falsehood, cheating and cruel actions (this graha's own signification, distinct from the Moon's own dasha below); tranquility of mind, success in business, good food, acquisition of wife, children, ornaments, clothes, gems, cows and lands; honours brahmins
results_by_graha.Mars: wealth through fire, the king, fighting and the like; money through administering medicines, falsehood, cheating and cruel actions; afflicted by bilious complaints and impurity of blood and fever; intrigues with low women; quarrels with wife, children, relations and elders; takes delight in others' misfortune
results_by_graha.Mercury: meeting of friends; personal comforts; fame through the applause of the learned; favour from elders; cleverness in speech; does good to others; happiness to one's wife and children and friends; an exalted position
results_by_graha.Jupiter: performs some virtuous deed; acquires children (suppressed); honoured by the sovereign; receives praise from great men; acquisition of elephants, horses and vehicles; meeting of wife, children and friends; fulfilment of one's desires
results_by_graha.Venus: obtains materials and facilities for sport and happiness; good vehicles, cows, gems, ornaments, treasure; enjoyment in the company of young women; intellectual pursuits; voyage; auspicious deeds; acceptance of presents from the sovereign
results_by_graha.Saturn: wife and children (suppressed) troubled by gout, rheumatism or similar windy diseases; loss in agriculture; evil talk; intercourse with wicked women; desertion by servants; absence from his own residence; sudden destruction or loss of relations, lands, happiness and wealth
results_by_graha.Rahu_general: trouble from the sovereign, thieves, poison, fire and weapons; sickness to children (suppressed); a ruffled mind; loss of relations; insult from base people; scandal from a breach of decorum; ejection or dismissal from office; injury to the leg; failure of the business undertaken
results_by_graha.Rahu_if_well_associated: if Rahu is associated with a benefic and occupies a good house (other than the 6th, 8th or 12th), the dasha is fully auspicious and lifts the native to affluence on a par with a king, with desires fulfilled and steady accumulation of wealth and wide renown
results_by_graha.Rahu_if_in_kanya_meena_vrischika: confers honour and happiness, lordship of lands, carriages and servants during Rahu's own dasha, though these gains are liable to be lost at the dasha's close
results_by_graha.Ketu: troubles from enemies, thieves, the sovereign; wounds from weapons; disease from excessive heat; false calumny; a stigma to his family; danger from fire; absence from his own country

exceptions: Only the Sun's result is explicitly conditioned on the natal placement's quality ('badly placed' vs 'well placed at birth') in this passage; the other eight grahas' results are stated unconditionally in Adhyaya XIX, distinct from (and not to be confused with) the placement-conditioned bhava results of Adhyaya VIII.
These are MAHADASHA-level (not antardasha/bhukti-level) significations; the source's antardasha subdivision material (Adhyaya XX-XXI) was not inspected in this pass.
Progeny/children clauses for Jupiter, Saturn and Rahu are suppressed as fertility-adjacent per this file's global policy.

The engine already computes the running mahadasha lord (`vimshottari_current.mahadasha.lord` in src/engine/multitradition/vedic.py's `build()` output) so this table is directly attachable to that field; no new calculation is required, only composer wiring.
